title: groundstation field test №14: the 18 cards stops 10 to 16 set out to fix, re-run on 0.35.0
heading: THE FIELD TEST №14
sub: groundstation · 18 prompts re-run · 8 live artifacts: 3 3D views, 2 postcards, 2 maps, 1 swipe · 7 fixed, 5 partly, 6 the same · October 26, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: The 18 cards from field tests 12 and 13 that stops 10 to 16 were charted to fix, asked again in the same words on main at 0.35.0 (PRs 69 to 75, one stop each, all merged this morning UTC), plus the 4 findings nobody charted yet. Each learning opens with the verdict: 7 fixed, 5 partly, 6 the same. Fixed: the ERA5 and MUR stores now say what they hold and refuse a date outside it with the range named; HRRR refuses a snap of more than one step instead of answering the wrong day; every pass carries daylight and sun elevation and the night optical passes are counted; the Mt Bachelor 3D view loads at 100% with the same-day sibling draped; the Phoenix postcard is the heat crop that was asked for and the Casco Bay postcard honours its box; Lake Charles is the city again and Lake Powell is the reservoir first. Partly: the WorldCover legend is there with 11 classes but the 6 layers still share one name; statistics say in words that Sentinel-2 scale and offset are unapplied, which is the caveat stop 12 promised and not the fix; the Cooley pass does not name which 2 night passes it dropped; the brief page and conditions_brief still pad by 0.4 and 1.5 degrees; Lake Powell, Utah is still a box far larger than Wahweap. The same: the Berkeley Pit candidate carries its tight box and the top-level bbox is still the 0.3 degree point-rule box; the Portland refusal still names no state, because that rule reaches Nominatim candidates and Gazet is what answers a bare name; a MODIS tile that is empty over the Central Valley is still the recommendation at covers_aoi_pct 92.6; compare_dates still has no out_path and no renderer has a place for a caller's own notes; and the Valencia tile flip did not reproduce in 3 identical runs, which is not evidence it is gone. New since 13: date-only windows that worked on field test 13 now raise an uncaught HTTP 400 in compare_dates, and the Casco Bay card is about 45% no-data behind a covers_aoi_pct of 100, which measures box overlap, not pixels. One phone-width screenshot (390 px) of the Lake Victoria legend is on its card. Every returned block is verbatim tool output and every card keeps its stumble. A field test is a showcase, not CI: it shows what the tools do today.

cases.answer: Not computable from this ERA5 store, and now the tools say so up front. Both October dates (2026-10-15 12Z and 2025-10-15 12Z) are refused by compute_statistics and tile_url_template with the same message: the time is outside the store's range, 1959-01-01 to 2023-01-10T18:00, and no statistics or tile URL come back. cases.learning: Fixed. Earlier: tile_url_template "accepted a 2026 time with no warning" and compute_statistics snapped to 2023-01-10 18:00 "off by 1373 days" with only a caveat, returning a January temperature to an October question. Now both tools refuse with the store's range in the message and return no numbers and no URL (seen above for 2026 and 2025, statistics and tile). Unverified: I asked for total_precipitation (the earlier name) and the range check fired before any variable check, so I did not see what a wrong variable name now says; and I ran no in-range precipitation read, so the metres unit is from the description only. Not re-run: the earlier card's other trap, "Sacramento Valley" geocoding to a train station; the valley box was set by hand again.

cases.answer: There is no usable Sentinel-2 pass over Longyearbyen in the next 3 days: the tool kept none, and counted 53 optical passes it dropped because the sun was below the horizon. Every pass it did return is radar (Sentinel-1A and 1C, NISAR), each with daylight: false and a sun elevation between -3.7 and -23.6 degrees, so the answer to worth it is no for optical, and radar is the instrument that works in this dark. Now each pass carries sun_elevation_deg and daylight, and the result carries optical_passes_at_night: 53, so the dark optical passes are counted instead of silently listed or silently missing. The Sentinel-2 rows that used to show at 12:29 UTC are gone from the list, which matches the earlier hand arithmetic of about -1.6 degrees. One thing to read carefully: this run is a day later than the old one, so the pass list is not the same set; the verdict rests on the new fields, not on a row-for-row diff.
